question: Can agreement between fixed history-based forecast models reduce harmful routing changes while retaining benefits under synthetic trend changes, measurement noise and timestamped latency?
evidence_status: Known-fire development plus frozen-seed synthetic stress confirmation. Synthetic perturbations are not new physically validated fires.

generator.shared_source: One original public FER field, 58 distinct region labels and 61 nonexit graph cells
generator.spatial_shape: Two seeded random region centres. Weight exp(-0.5*(region graph distance / width)^2), width uniform[2,5] graph moves; shared region cells receive identical rates
generator.accelerating_local: Two nonnegative local additions: amplitude * clip((t-onset)/120,0,1)^2; persistent thereafter
generator.transient_local: Two nonnegative triangular pulses, independent seeded rise and fall durations uniform[30,90] seconds
generator.noise: Mean-one multiplicative lognormal noise, standard deviation / mean = noise_cv, independent by region and native sample; reuse standard normal draws across matched sensor arms
generator.latency: Native acquisition timestamps retained; only samples with acquisition+latency <= decision time are delivered. Never mislabel stale data as current.
generator.normalization: No full-fire statistics used to choose perturbation amplitudes or online model parameters
generator.physical_claim: Mathematical stress fields only; no claim to satisfy combustion or smoke-transport equations

gate.nominee: Full fixed plan from the arithmetic mean of the three forecast interval-cost matrices
gate.comparator: Full snapshot-optimal fixed plan from the same state/time/deadline
gate.score: Score the SAME nominee and SAME comparator under each forecast model; minimum relative predicted FED gain across models
gate.application: Only a different first action is a gate opportunity. Execute first action and replan; rejection executes snapshot first action.
gate.uncertainty_interpretation: Forecast-model disagreement, not a calibrated predictive confidence interval or safety guarantee
gate.fixed_cost_accounting: No added dose penalty or action mask; switching thresholds are heuristic and tested for possible harm

execution.context: Original clean source at four departures once; diagnostic only
execution.development: 4 seeds x 14 arms = 56 worlds; 9 methods including two threshold sensitivities
execution.confirmation: 60 fresh seeds x 14 arms = 840 worlds; seven primary methods unchanged
execution.generation_order: Context, development, then confirmation. All method, threshold, generator and seed hashes frozen before any new scoring; no method selection between stages.
execution.memory: Process and write one world at a time; gzip traces, npz policy tables; no LLM model loading
execution.resume: Completed world manifests must verify; never overwrite completed world outputs
execution.stop: After the planned matrix, independent audit and one report; do not expand the matrix based on a favorable or unfavorable result

evaluation.gate_confusion: At each gate opportunity visited by that gated policy, use offline truth to compare one nominee action then snapshot continuation against snapshot continuation. Count rejected beneficial and accepted harmful opportunities separately; overlapping opportunities are not independent outcomes.
evaluation.fairness: All online methods share map, acquisition/delivery timestamps, measured histories, action constraints, deadline and objective; gates use more planning work, which is reported. Oracle has future information and is only a reference.
evaluation.confirmation_statement: Only fresh generator/noise seed confirmation. Shared base fire, topology and generator prohibit claims of independent-fire generalization.
evaluation.statistics: Descriptive arm and world aggregates; no trajectory-level independent-sample significance tests
evaluation.failure: Never count partial FED as low-dose success; report arrivals and jointly reached comparisons
